title: News and society
focus: sorkar, niti, orthoniti, nirbachon, ain, andolon, michhil, mulyobriddhi, bekarotto, dushon, songbad madhyam, durniti, songskar, unnoyon, bandh
body:
# News and society

Family talk rarely touches politics or the economy, but the news, the adda at the tea stall and any serious conversation do. These are the words of Bengali news channels and newspapers, with notes on what people actually say in a Kolkata living room.

| Romanization | Bengali | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| sorkar | সরকার | government (the state) |
| niti | নীতি | policy (government or company) |
| orthoniti | অর্থনীতি | economy / economics |
| nirbachon | নির্বাচন | election |
| ain | আইন | law (a law, the law) |
| andolon | আন্দোলন | movement / agitation (political or social campaign) |
| michhil | মিছিল | procession / protest march |
| mulyobriddhi | মূল্যবৃদ্ধি | inflation / rise in prices (formal) |
| bekarotto | বেকারত্ব | unemployment |
| dushon | দূষণ | pollution |
| poribesh | পরিবেশ | environment (natural) |
| somaj | সমাজ | society |
| songbad madhyam | সংবাদমাধ্যম | the news media / the press |
| durniti | দুর্নীতি | corruption |
| songskar | সংস্কার | reform (of a system) |
| unnoyon | উন্নয়ন | development (of a region, infrastructure) |
| bandh | বনধ | general strike / shutdown (called by a party) |
| birodhi dol | বিরোধী দল | opposition (party) |
| shashok dol | শাসক দল | ruling party |
| montri | মন্ত্রী | minister |
| nagorik | নাগরিক | citizen |
| odhikar | অধিকার | right(s) (legal, civil) |
| protibad | প্রতিবাদ | protest (an act of objecting) |
| hingsa | হিংসা | violence (news) |
| adalot | আদালত | court (of law) |
| ray | রায় | verdict / ruling (of a court) |
| porikathamo | পরিকাঠামো | infrastructure (WB usage) |
| jonogon | জনগণ | the public / the people |

## Which word?

- **andolon vs protibad vs michhil**: andolon is a sustained movement; protibad is a single act of protest or objection; michhil is the march on the street.
- **mulyobriddhi vs dam bere geche**: mulyobriddhi is the news word for inflation; at home people say "sob kichhur dam bere geche".
- **nirbachon vs bhot**: nirbachon is the formal word; in speech people say bhot (vote) for both the vote and the election.
- **bandh vs bondho**: bandh (বনধ) is a called strike or shutdown; bondho (বন্ধ) just means closed.
- **hingsa vs hingse**: hingsa in the news is violence; hingse in conversation is jealousy.
- **songbad madhyam vs media**: in speech almost everyone says media.

## Examples

- sorkar notun prokolpo ghoshona korechhe: the government has announced a new scheme
- desh-er orthoniti-r obostha bhalo na: the country's economy isn't in good shape
- chakri-r dabi-te chhatra-ra andolon korchhe: students are agitating for jobs
- Dharmatala-y michhil-er jonno rasta bondho: the road is closed at Dharmatala because of a march
- rajje bekarotto ekta boro somossa: unemployment is a big problem in the state
- shiter somoy Kolkata-y bayu dushon bhishon bere jay: air pollution gets terrible in winter
- durniti-r obhijoge montri-ke greftar kora hoyechhe: the minister was arrested on corruption charges
- unnoyon-er naam-e gachh kata hochchhe: trees are being cut in the name of development
- kal bandh daka hoyechhe: a bandh has been called for tomorrow
- byapar-ta ekhon adalot-e: the matter is now in court

cards.Example: sorkar notun prokolpo ghoshona korechhe: the government has announced a new scheme
cards.Notes: sorkari = governmental, public (sorkari hashpatal = government hospital).

cards.Example: sorkar-er shikkha niti niye onek torko hochchhe: there's a lot of debate about the government's education policy
cards.Notes: Also 'principle' (nitibodh = moral sense). 'policy' is common in office talk.

cards.Example: nirbachon-er aage shohor jure prochar cholchhe: campaigning is on across the city before the election
cards.Notes: In speech often 'bhot' (vote): bhot kobe? = when's the election?

cards.Example: notun ain-e ei niyom bodle geche: under the new law this rule has changed
cards.Notes: ain bhanga = to break the law; ainjibi = lawyer (spoken: ukil).

cards.Example: chakri-r dabi-te chhatra-ra andolon korchhe: students are agitating for jobs
cards.Notes: A sustained campaign; protibad is a single act of protest.

cards.Example: Dharmatala-y michhil-er jonno rasta bondho: the road is closed at Dharmatala because of a march
cards.Notes: A Kolkata staple; 'rally' is also used. michhil is the march itself.

cards.Example: mulyobriddhi-r chap-e madhyobitto-ra nakal: the middle class is squeezed by inflation
cards.Notes: News word. In conversation: 'jinishpotro-r dam bere geche'.

cards.Example: shiter somoy Kolkata-y bayu dushon bhishon bere jay: air pollution in Kolkata gets terrible in winter
cards.Notes: bayu dushon = air pollution; sobdo dushon = noise pollution; poribesh dushon = environmental pollution.

cards.Example: plastic poribesh-er jonno khub khotikor: plastic is very harmful for the environment
cards.Notes: Also 'atmosphere' of a place (bari-r poribesh = home atmosphere).

cards.Example: somaj-er chokhe eta ekhono mene newa hoy na: society still doesn't accept this
cards.Notes: samajik = social; 'lok ki bolbe' is the everyday version of social pressure.

cards.Example: songbad madhyam ghotona-ta niye chup: the media is silent on the incident
cards.Notes: In speech just 'media'. songbad = news (formal); khobor is everyday.

cards.Example: durniti-r obhijoge montri-ke greftar kora hoyechhe: the minister was arrested on corruption charges
cards.Notes: durnitigrosto = corrupt (formal); spoken 'ghushkhor' for a person who takes bribes.

cards.Example: shikkha byabostha-y songskar dorkar: the education system needs reform
cards.Notes: Also means repair/renovation (bari songskar) and, in another sense, custom or superstition.

cards.Example: unnoyon-er naam-e gachh kata hochchhe: trees are being cut in the name of development
cards.Notes: A key word in West Bengal politics; 'development' is also used.

cards.English: general strike / shutdown (called by a party)
cards.Example: kal bandh daka hoyechhe: a bandh has been called for tomorrow
cards.Notes: Spelled বনধ to distinguish it from বন্ধ (closed). bandh daka = to call a bandh.

cards.Example: birodhi dol bidhansobha theke walkout korlo: the opposition walked out of the assembly
cards.Notes: birodhi = opposing; dol = party/group.

cards.Example: shashok dol-er neta-ra ei obhijog oswikar korechhe: ruling party leaders have denied the allegation
cards.Notes: News phrase; in speech people just name the party.

cards.Example: montri nije ese elaka-ta dekhe gechhen: the minister came and inspected the area himself
cards.Notes: mukhyomontri = chief minister; prodhanmontri = prime minister.

cards.Example: protyek nagorik-er bhot dewa uchit: every citizen should vote
cards.Notes: nagorikotto = citizenship.

cards.Example: eta amader odhikar, keu kere nite parbe na: this is our right, no one can take it away
cards.Notes: odhikar also covers 'claim, entitlement' (ogradhikar = priority).

cards.Example: obichar dekhle protibad korte hobe: when you see injustice you must speak up
cards.Notes: protibad kora = to protest, also to object in a conversation.

cards.Example: bhot-er por elaka-y hingsa chhoriye pore: violence broke out in the area after the vote
cards.Notes: Do not confuse with spoken hingse (jealousy). Both are হিংসা in writing; context decides.

cards.Example: byapar-ta ekhon adalot-e: the matter is now in court
cards.Notes: Spoken: 'court' (court-e mamla cholchhe). mamla = lawsuit/case.

cards.Example: High Court ajke ray debe: the High Court will give its ruling today
cards.Notes: ray dewa = to deliver a verdict. Also a common surname (Ray / Roy).

cards.Example: jelar hashpatal-gulo-r porikathamo khub kharap: the district hospitals have very poor infrastructure
cards.Notes: West Bengal word; Bangladesh says obokathamo.

cards.Example: shesh porjonto jonogon-i thik korbe: in the end the people will decide
cards.Notes: Formal; in speech 'sadharon manush' (ordinary people) is common.

cards.English: Everything will be shut tomorrow because of the bandh.
cards.Romanization: kal bandh-er jonno sob bondho thakbe
cards.Bengali: কাল বনধের জন্য সব বন্ধ থাকবে
cards.Notes: Note the pun: bandh (strike) makes everything bondho (closed).

cards.English: Prices of everything have shot up.
cards.Notes: The everyday way to talk about inflation; mulyobriddhi is the news word.
